chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from Yūnus, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who gave birth and then saw blood for longer than she used to see. He said: “She should refrain for the days of her menstrual period during which she used to sit, then take a precaution up to ten days. If she sees flowing blood, then she should perform ghusl at the time of every salat (prayer); and if she sees yellowish discharge, then she should perform wudu (ablution) and then pray.”
His saying عليه السلام, “she takes precaution with ten days,” means up to ten days, because particles of attribution can stand in the place of one another.

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she takes precaution by extending consideration up to a limit
key_terms.فَلْتَغْتَسِلْ: then she should perform ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.قُرْئِهَا: her established menstrual period or cycle

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman whose postnatal bleeding continues longer than her usual menstrual period?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning postnatal bleeding and how a woman distinguishes between the days corresponding to her known menstrual habit and what follows after that. It explains the practical rulings for salat (prayer), ghusl, and wudu (ablution) based on the nature of the blood seen, and it also clarifies the wording “with ten days” as meaning “up to ten days.”
